q165.question: What is meant by the statement that Paradise "exists without time and has no location in space"?
q165.answer:
Paradise is the center of the universe and the dwelling place of God, but it is not one more heavenly body bound by the laws of time and space. The Urantia Book says: "⟦Q 11:2.10⟧O Paraíso existe fora do tempo e não tem localização no espaço.⟦/Q⟧" [11:2.10]. This does not mean that Paradise is set somewhere within space; rather, it means that space and time arise and unfold with Paradise as their point of reference.

In other words, Paradise is less a place within the universe than the absolute point of reference that makes the universe possible. Thus the book calls Paradise "⟦Q 11:9.2⟧the geographic center of infinity⟦/Q⟧" [11:9.2], yet says that it is neither a part of universal creation nor even a real part of the eternal Havona universe, but "⟦Q 11:9.2⟧an eternal and exclusive existence⟦/Q⟧" [11:9.2].

1. Paradise Is Not in Space but Is the Source of Space

Space does not exist on any of the surfaces of Paradise; space does not touch Paradise directly, and only the quiescent midspace zones come in contact with the central Isle [11:7.1]. Space is neither the presence of the Unqualified Absolute nor a function of the Ultimate; "⟦Q 11:7.4⟧it is a bestowal of Paradise⟦/Q⟧" [11:7.4]. Roughly speaking, space seemingly originates just below nether Paradise, and time just above upper Paradise [11:2.11]. Paradise, therefore, is not an object in space but the place from which space proceeds.

2. No Time, Yet a Sequence of Events

Time as we understand it is not a feature of Paradise existence, yet the citizens of the central Isle are fully conscious of the "⟦Q 11:2.11⟧nontime sequence of events⟦/Q⟧" [11:2.11]. Motion, too, is not inherent on Paradise; it is volitional [11:2.11]. To say that there is no time does not mean that nothing happens, but that things happen without being subject to the flow of time. Moreover, the concept of distance, even absolute distance, has very much meaning as it may be applied to relative locations on Paradise [11:2.11].

3. A Unique Source Material: Absolutum

The eternal Isle is composed of a homogeneous organization of space potency not to be found elsewhere in all the universe of universes, and the Melchizedeks of Nebadon named it absolutum [11:2.9]. This Paradise source material is neither dead nor alive; it is the original nonspiritual expression of the First Source and Center [11:2.9]. The Universal Father appears to have concentrated all absolute potential for cosmic reality in Paradise as a means of making possible subinfinite, even time-space, creation [11:2.10]. But it does not follow that Paradise is time-space limited just because the universes disclose time-space qualities [11:2.10].

4. Not Deity, Yet the Source-Center of All Things

When the Father revealed the infinite personality expression of his spirit self in the Eternal Son, he simultaneously revealed the infinite potential of his nonpersonal self as Paradise [11:9.3]. Paradise is therefore nonpersonal and nonspiritual, and the book states plainly that "⟦Q 11:9.4⟧Paradise is not Deity⟦/Q⟧" [11:9.4]. Nevertheless, Paradise is the universal headquarters of all personality activities and the source-center of all force-space and energy manifestations [11:9.7]. Paradise is also the absolute of patterns, and Havona is an exhibit of these potentials in actuality [11:9.5].

5. What It Means for Us

What matters most for mortals is that this dwelling place of the Father, beyond time and space, is the real and far-distant destiny of the immortal souls of ascending creatures [11:9.8]. Every God-knowing mortal who has embraced the career of doing the Father's will has already embarked upon the Paradise journey [11:9.8]. The very fact that we who live in time and space set our goal on a place beyond time and space shows that human destiny is not confined to the material world.

Summary

Paradise is not an island set in space but the nonspatial and timeless center from which space and time proceed [11:2.10, 11:7.4]. There is a sequence of events and meaning of location there, but no flow of time and no limitation of space [11:2.11]. Paradise is not Deity, yet it is the source-center of all energy and personality activity [11:9.4, 11:9.7], and it is the final destination at which every God-knowing mortal will at last arrive [11:9.8].

q166.question: What is the "space respiration" spoken of in The Urantia Book, and what does it mean that space alternately expands and contracts?
q166.answer:
The Urantia Book says that all space is observed alternately to contract and expand, and it calls this "space respiration" [11:6.1]. While the horizontal pervaded space in which the universes are situated expands, the vertical reservoir space above and below Paradise contracts, and vice versa [11:6.2]. Each phase lasts a little more than one billion Urantia years, and a complete cycle of expansion and contraction takes a little more than two billion years [11:6.4-5].

What is noteworthy in this teaching is that the revelators themselves frankly state, "⟦Q 11:6.1⟧We do not know the actual mechanism of space respiration⟦/Q⟧" [11:6.1], and report only the observed facts.

1. Two Kinds of Space: Pervaded Space and Unpervaded Space

Pervaded space: the space that contains the universes, extending horizontally outward from near approach to peripheral Paradise through the fourth outer space level and beyond [11:6.4, 11:7.4]. This space is believed to be actually pervaded by the ancestral space potency of the Unqualified Absolute [11:7.4].

Unpervaded space: space "⟦Q 11:6.3⟧unpervaded by those forces, energies, powers, and presences known to exist in pervaded space⟦/Q⟧" [11:6.3]; these are the reservoirs extending vertically above upper Paradise and below nether Paradise [11:6.4].

The book compares the volume outlines of these reservoirs to an hourglass [11:6.1]. It also says that a vertical cross section of all space would resemble a Maltese cross, the horizontal arms representing pervaded (universe) space and the vertical arms representing unpervaded (reservoir) space [11:7.3].

2. Where the Respiration Takes Place

The junction of pervaded and unpervaded space lies just underneath nether Paradise. Both spaces flow through the transmuting regulation channels there, and in the cycles of contraction and expansion pervadable space is changed into unpervadable space and vice versa [11:6.2]. Yet there is no space on the surfaces of Paradise; only the quiescent midspace zones are in contact with the Isle [11:7.1], and Paradise is the motionless nucleus of the relatively quiet zones existing between pervaded and unpervaded space [11:7.2].

3. Which Phase Are We in Now?

At present, pervaded space is approaching the mid-point of the phase of expansion, while unpervaded space nears the mid-point of the phase of contraction [11:6.4]. Theoretically, the outermost limits of both space extensions are now approximately equidistant from Paradise [11:6.4]. For one billion years, while the force activities of the master universe and of all horizontal space expand, the space reservoirs contract [11:6.5].

4. An Order for Balance and Stability

The book says that it does not know whether reservoir space is destined always to function as the equipoise of universe space, or whether there is a creative intent concerning it, yet it says that the reservoirs seem to counterbalance the expansion-contraction cycles of the universe of universes [11:6.3]. Again, the quiet zones between the space levels and the alternate clockwise and counterclockwise flows of the galaxies are physical gravity stabilizers that keep gravity pressure from accumulating to the point of destructive activities; they exert antigravity influences and act as brakes upon dangerous velocities [11:7.9]. Here we can glimpse how even the rhythms of space are woven in orderly fashion around Paradise.

Summary

Space respiration is a vast cycle in which the horizontal pervaded space containing the universes and the vertical unpervaded space above and below Paradise alternately expand and contract [11:6.1-2]. One phase lasts a little more than a billion years and a whole cycle a little more than two billion years [11:6.4-5], and pervaded space is now approaching the middle of its expansion phase [11:6.4]. Even the revelators do not know its mechanism, but its rhythm is understood as part of the balance and stability of the universe centered on Paradise [11:6.3, 11:7.9].

q167.question: What are the four absolute gravity circuits, personality gravity, spirit gravity, mind gravity, and physical gravity, and how do they differ?
q167.answer:
The Urantia Book says that all forms of force-energy, whether material, mindal, or spiritual, are alike subject to the grasp of that universal presence which we call "gravity," and that personality also is responsive to gravity, to the Father's exclusive circuit [12:3.1]. In other words, gravity is not merely a force by which bodies attract one another; it is a fourfold presence by which the Deities draw all the realities of the universe to themselves.

The four circuits are the personality gravity of the Universal Father, the spirit gravity of the Eternal Son, the mind gravity of the Conjoint Actor, and the cosmic gravity of the Isle of Paradise [12:3.2-5]. These four circuits are not related to the nether Paradise force center; they are not circuits of force, energy, or power, but "⟦Q 12:3.6⟧Eles são circuitos de presença absoluta e, como Deus, são independentes do tempo e do espaço.⟦/Q⟧" [12:3.6]. The corps of gravity researchers on Uversa have estimated how much of each circuit is now operating in the universe [12:3.7], and their findings illustrate well the differences among the four circuits.

1. Physical Gravity: The Cosmic Gravity of the Isle of Paradise

According to the researchers' computations, the central universe and the seven superuniverses are at present using only about five per cent of the active functioning of the Paradise absolute-gravity grasp [12:3.8]. The remaining ninety-five per cent or so is engaged in controlling material systems beyond the borders of the present organized universes [12:3.8]. These calculations all refer to absolute gravity; linear gravity is an interactive phenomenon which can be computed only by knowing the actual Paradise gravity [12:3.8].

2. Spirit Gravity: The Drawing Power of the Eternal Son

By the same technique, the total spirit gravity of the Eternal Son was computed and found to be almost exactly equal to the spirit gravity actually functioning in the grand universe [12:3.9]. This means that the universes now evolving in outer space are at present wholly nonspiritual, and it explains why spirit-endowed beings know so little about those vast energy manifestations [12:3.9].

3. Mind Gravity: The Intellectual Drawing of the Conjoint Actor

The researchers averaged three types of material mind and three types of spiritual mind to obtain a unit of mind estimation [12:3.10], and they deduced that about eighty-five per cent of the mind-gravity response originates in the existing grand universe [12:3.10]. The remainder suggests the possibility that mind activities are connected with the physical activities in outer space, which agrees with the belief that intelligent force organizers are directing universe evolution beyond the grand universe. That intelligence, however, appears not to be responsive to spirit gravity [12:3.10]. All these computations are estimates based on assumed laws, yet they are said to be fairly reliable [12:3.11].

4. Personality Gravity: The Father's Exclusive Circuit

"⟦Q 12:3.12⟧A Gravidade da Personalidade não é calculável.⟦/Q⟧" [12:3.12]. The circuit is recognized, but the realities responsive to it cannot be measured either qualitatively or quantitatively [12:3.12]. This circuit is exclusive to the Father, but he is not excluded from the other circuits; being infinite, he acts over all four absolute-gravity circuits [12:3.1].

5. What This Means for Our Faith

The fact that the personality circuit is exclusive to the Father means that every personality is held directly by the Father. The book says that the Father's love individualizes each personality as "⟦Q 12:7.9⟧a child without duplicate in infinity⟦/Q⟧" [12:7.9], and it comforts us: "⟦Q 12:7.12⟧the Father is not very far from any one of you⟦/Q⟧" [12:7.12]. As physical gravity holds the stars, so personality gravity, in a way that cannot be measured, is drawing us to the Father.

Summary

The four absolute gravity circuits are the personality gravity of the Father, the spirit gravity of the Son, the mind gravity of the Conjoint Actor, and the physical gravity of Paradise, and all are absolute presence circuits independent of time and space [12:3.2-6]. Physical gravity acts mostly beyond the organized universes [12:3.8], spirit gravity functions almost wholly in the grand universe [12:3.9], and about eighty-five per cent of mind gravity originates in the grand universe [12:3.10]. Personality gravity alone is the Father's circuit, which cannot be measured [12:3.12].

q168.question: What does the teaching of "the part and the whole" mean, that the will of God does not necessarily prevail in one person's heart but does rule the universe as a whole?
q168.answer:
The Urantia Book says: "⟦Q 12:7.1⟧A misericórdia caracteriza a atitude do amor de Deus pelo indivíduo; a imparcialidade motiva a atitude de Deus para com a totalidade.⟦/Q⟧" [12:7.1]. And it explains that the will of God does not necessarily prevail in the part, the heart of any one personality, but does rule the whole, the universe of universes [12:7.1]. This means that God does not force individuals who possess free will, but the direction of the whole universe is firmly maintained within his will.

This teaching can be understood from three aspects: the laws of God and freedom, the individual and the community, and the growth of faith in time.

1. The Laws of God Are Not Arbitrary

Throughout all time and space there is operative an impersonal law equivalent to the function of a cosmic providence [12:7.1]. To our limited vision the acts of God may appear dictatorial and arbitrary, but "⟦Q 12:7.2⟧The laws of God are merely the habits of God⟦/Q⟧" [12:7.2], simply his best way of repeatedly doing things. The book also asks us to remember that nature is not the exclusive act of Deity; other influences are present in those phenomena which man calls nature [12:7.2].

2. God Is Not a Slave to Law

God is not a self-acting automatic force or a law-bound power; "⟦Q 12:7.6⟧He is a freewill and primal personality⟦/Q⟧" [12:7.6]. Thus, if a better way is called for in a certain situation, God functions in that way, and this is not the overriding of a lower law but the expression of a higher law [12:7.3]. Because he is changeless, we can depend on him to act in the same way in ordinary situations, and he is the guarantee of the stability of all created things and beings [12:7.5].

3. The Longer the Time, the More the Will of God Is Revealed

The will of God does not uniformly prevail in the heart of the God-seeking mortal, but as the time frame is enlarged from a single moment to the whole of the first life, the will of God becomes increasingly discernible in the spirit fruits borne in the lives of the spirit-led [12:7.7]. And as it is further enlarged to include morontia experience, that will shines ever more brightly [12:7.7]. This is an encouragement not to lose heart over today's failures but to look at the whole of the long ascending journey.

4. Fatherhood and Brotherhood: The Paradox of the Part and the Whole

"⟦Q 12:7.8⟧A Paternidade de Deus e a fraternidade do homem apresentam o paradoxo da parte e do todo, no nível da personalidade.⟦/Q⟧" [12:7.8]. God loves each person as an individual child in the heavenly family, yet he so loves every individual, and the universality of his love brings into being the universal brotherhood [12:7.8, 12:7.10]. The Father's love absolutely individualizes each personality as a will creature irreplaceable in all eternity [12:7.9].

5. My Good Deeds and My Errors Affect Everyone

Since brotherhood is a fact of relationship between every personality in universal existence, no person can escape the benefits or the penalties that come from relationship to other persons [12:7.11]. "⟦Q 12:7.11⟧O bom esforço, de cada homem, beneficia a todos os homens; o mal ou o erro, de cada homem, aumenta a atribulação de todos os homens.⟦/Q⟧" [12:7.11]. As moves the part, so moves the whole; and as the progress of the whole, so the progress of the part [12:7.11]. Therefore an individual's life of faith never remains a merely private matter.

6. The Father Who Is Far Away and Yet Nearest of All

It is a mystery that God has his residential headquarters on Paradise and at the same time is personally in contact with a well-nigh infinite number of beings in a vast universe, but this should not weaken our faith [12:7.12]. The Father dwells within you, and the fragment of the Father in the mortal mind holds mysterious communion with the human soul [12:7.12-13].

Summary

God deals with the individual in mercy and with the whole in impartiality [12:7.1]. His will does not always prevail in the heart of a single person endowed with free will, but it rules the whole universe and is revealed ever more clearly over the long time of ascension [12:7.1, 12:7.7]. Because God loves each person uniquely, all become brothers [12:7.9-10], and so one person's goodness and errors affect the whole [12:7.11].

q169.question: What is each of the Father's seven sacred worlds that circle Paradise like, and why are so many secrets kept there?
q169.answer:
Between Paradise and Havona the satellite spheres of Paradise circle in three circuits, and the innermost of these circuits is the Father's seven sacred worlds [13:1.1]. These worlds contain "⟦Q 13:1.1⟧the only inherent personality secrets in the universe of universes⟦/Q⟧" [13:1.1], and they are directed by the Trinitized Secrets of Supremacy, the highest order of the Stationary Sons of the Trinity [13:1.2].

One reason these worlds are secret is that each sphere enjoys a specialized expression of the Deities composing the Paradise Trinity, a unique presence of divinity that can be recognized and understood only by the particular groups who reside on it or are admitted to it [13:1.3].

1. The Seven Worlds and Their Secrets

Divinington: the "⟦Q 13:1.4⟧bosom of the Father⟦/Q⟧" and the Paradise rendezvous of the Thought Adjusters. The bestowal and mission of the Adjusters, their nature and origin, and their technique of contact with human beings are the secrets of this world [13:1.4-5].

Sonarington: the "⟦Q 13:1.7⟧bosom of the Son⟦/Q⟧" and the Paradise headquarters of the descending and ascending Sons of God. The incarnation of the divine Sons is its secret [13:1.7-8].

Spiritington: the "⟦Q 13:1.9⟧bosom of the Spirit⟦/Q⟧," where the Seven Master Spirits and certain of their offspring forgather; the mysteries of reflectivity are its secret [13:1.9-10].

Vicegerington: the "⟦Q 13:1.11⟧bosom of the Father and the Son⟦/Q⟧," which keeps the secrets of trinitization, that is, the secrets of the authority to represent the Trinity [13:1.11-12].

Solitarington: the "⟦Q 13:1.15⟧bosom of the Father and the Spirit⟦/Q⟧," the home of the Solitary Messengers, and in the present universe age also the status sphere of the Universe Power Directors [13:1.15-16].

Seraphington: the "⟦Q 13:1.19⟧bosom of the Son and the Spirit⟦/Q⟧," the destiny sphere of all ministering orders of the angelic hosts, which keeps the mysteries of seraphic transport [13:1.19-20].

Ascendington: the "⟦Q 13:1.21⟧bosom of the Father, Son, and Spirit⟦/Q⟧," the rendezvous of the ascendant creatures, which keeps the mystery of the evolution of the immortal soul within the mortal mind [13:1.21-22].

2. Secrets Are Not Discrimination but the Protection of Trust

The revelator says that if the truths of Divinington were revealed, they would rather confuse him in his work, and might even exceed the conceptual capacity of his order of being [13:1.6]. And "⟦Q 13:2.8⟧Quando o Criador tem um segredo de personalidade experiencial com a sua criatura, o Criador preserva esse segredo em confiança eterna.⟦/Q⟧" [13:2.8]. Secrets, in other words, are a way of respecting the unique experience of each order of beings.

3. Doors That Open to Mortals and Doors That Stay Closed

When mortals reach Havona they are granted admission to Ascendington, and after being mustered into the Corps of the Finality they may also enter Sonarington, but the one-seventh sector reserved for the secrets of incarnation will not be opened to them [13:2.6]. Eventually they will have relative access to the other spheres except Divinington, but they will never land on the shores of Divinington [13:2.7]. Yet the book adds that we shall surely stand repeatedly at the "⟦Q 13:2.7⟧right hand of the Father⟦/Q⟧" [13:2.7].

4. A Secret Belonging Only to Humans: Ascendington

Interestingly, one seventh of Ascendington is forbidden to the revelator, a high being of Trinity origin, because that sector holds the secret of an experience belonging only to beings of the human type, the fusion of the Adjuster with the human soul [13:1.23]. Even after it is revealed to us, that secret will remain our secret forever [13:1.23]. Ascendington will always be our home address, even when we serve in outer space, and it will be the home of our sentimental memories [13:2.1].

Summary

The Father's seven worlds are the "bosoms" and rendezvous of the Deities and of various orders of beings, and each keeps its own secrets, such as those of the Adjusters, of incarnation, of reflectivity, and of trinitization [13:1.4-22]. These secrets are an expression of trust that respects the experience of each order [13:2.8], and to mortals too is entrusted a secret known only to themselves, the mystery of the evolution of the immortal soul [13:1.22-23].

q170.question: Why does the eternal central universe of Havona exist, and what is life on Havona like?
q170.answer:
Havona is the eternal and perfect central universe surrounding Paradise. The Urantia Book broadly divides the activities of Havona into Havonal, Paradisiacal, and ascendant-finite activities [14:6.1-4], and explains that this perfect creation serves in different ways seven orders of universe intelligence, from the Deities to the ascending mortals [14:6.5]. At the same time the revelator adds that the central universe probably also contributes to many purposes that have not been revealed to him [14:6.5].

In a word, Havona is the joy of perfection to the Deities, the pattern for the evolutionary universes, and the gateway into Paradise for the ascenders.

1. What Havona Means to the Deities

God the Father derives supreme parental satisfaction from the perfection of Havona, and "⟦Q 14:6.6⟧O Criador Perfeito se compraz divinamente com a adoração da criatura perfeita.⟦/Q⟧" [14:6.6]. The realization of perfection in Havona compensates for the time-space delay in the urge of infinite expansion [14:6.7]. To the Eternal Son, Havona is the first and eternally final demonstration that the Son is the Word of the Father [14:6.15], and to the Infinite Spirit it was the stage of rehearsal for the ministry of mercy in the evolutionary universes [14:6.18]. Havona is also the eternal and perfect proof of the spiritual reality of the Supreme Being and foreshadows the future unification of the Supreme [14:6.23-24].

2. A Pattern and Training Ground for the Evolutionary Universes

Havona is the educational training ground in which the Creator Sons prepare for their adventures in universe creation, and a Creator Son strives that his universe may eventually attain this Paradise-Havona level of perfection [14:6.27]. The Universe Mother Spirits also receive their prepersonal training on the worlds of Havona [14:6.32]. The Havona worlds are the "mind laboratory" [14:6.20] that serves as the pattern for all creature minds, and they are the postgraduate school of mind for all beings destined to Paradise [14:6.21].

3. For Ascending Mortals Havona Is the Gateway

Havona is the pre-Paradise training goal of all ascending mortals, and here mortals attain the Supreme Being, the pre-Paradise Deity [14:6.38]. The book says, "⟦Q 14:6.39⟧O Paraíso é o lar, e Havona é a oficina, o local de estudos e lazer e a área de operações dos finalitores.⟦/Q⟧" [14:6.39]. Beginning on the seventh circuit, the ascenders progress toward the inner circuits, attaining in turn the Master Spirit, the Supreme, the Infinite Spirit, the Eternal Son, and the Universal Father [14:5.4]. Interestingly, the name "circles of progress" in the human mind is said to derive from this arrangement of Havona [14:5.4].

4. Life on Havona: A World without Monotony

Life on Havona is so rich and full that it transcends the human concept of anything a created being could experience, and even the technique of thinking differs from that of Urantia [14:5.2]. Its regulations are not arbitrary but natural, so that the ascender comes naturally to enjoy doing things in the way they ought to be done [14:5.3]. Each of the billion worlds is an original and unique creation [14:5.6], and "⟦Q 14:5.9⟧A monotonia não faz parte da carreira em Havona.⟦/Q⟧" [14:5.9].

5. The Lesson for Us Now

The book says that the love of adventure, curiosity, and the dread of monotony were not given to torment us, but to suggest that death is only the beginning of an endless career of adventure [14:5.10]. These urges are often repressed and disappointed on earth, but during the long ages to come they will be fully realized and gloriously gratified [14:5.11].

Summary

Havona gives the Deities the satisfaction of perfection, serves the Creator Sons and Mother Spirits as pattern and training ground, and is for all ascenders the gateway in which they attain the Supreme Being and enter Paradise [14:6.6, 14:6.27, 14:6.38]. Life there is full of endless surprises [14:5.9], and our curiosity and love of adventure are divine endowments given for that very eternal journey [14:5.10-11].

q171.question: How is the superuniverse government headed by the Ancients of Days organized and operated?
q171.answer:
The superuniverse headquarters is the seat of the high spiritual government of the time-space domains, and each superuniverse is presided over by three Ancients of Days, the joint supreme executives [15:10.1, 15:10.3]. The headquarters of our superuniverse, Orvonton, is Uversa. The superuniverse government has a unique structure in which an executive branch originating in the realms of perfection works together with a deliberative branch that has risen from the evolutionary universes [15:11.1].

1. Who Are the Ancients of Days?

The Ancients of Days are Supreme Trinity Personalities, all basically identical, and they disclose the combined character of the Trinity [18:3.2]. Whereas the Seven Master Spirits determine the nature of each superuniverse, the Ancients of Days dictate its administration, insuring uniformity of administration and the harmony of the whole among the seven differing superuniverses [18:3.3]. They were all trinitized at the same time, and the trinitization of these twenty-one beings is said to be the first record in the personality records of Paradise [18:3.4]. They always rule as a group of three [18:3.5].

2. The Seven Groups of the Executive Branch

The executive branch of the superuniverse government is composed of seven groups: the Ancients of Days, the Perfectors of Wisdom, the Divine Counselors, the Universal Censors, the Mighty Messengers, Those High in Authority, and Those without Name and Number [15:10.3-10]. The first three groups are co-ordinate Trinity personalities of direct origin in the Paradise Trinity [15:10.11]. The last three groups are glorified ascendant mortals who, after being mustered into the Corps of the Finality, were embraced by the Trinity and assigned to the service of the Ancients of Days [15:10.12]. "⟦Q 15:10.12⟧Assim, o ramo executivo do governo do superuniverso foi ampliado, para incluir os filhos glorificados e perfeccionados dos mundos evolucionários.⟦/Q⟧" [15:10.12].

3. The Deliberative Assembly: The Democracy of Evolution

The legislative or advisory council of the superuniverse consists of seven assemblies, and each local universe admitted to membership elects one native representative to each assembly [15:11.2]. These representatives are chosen from among the graduates of the Orvonton ascendant pilgrimage who are tarrying on Uversa, accredited for transport to Havona [15:11.2]. The revelator says he knows of no disagreement between the Orvonton executives and the Uversa assembly, and that this testifies that evolutionary beings can truly attain the heights of perfected wisdom [15:11.3].

4. The Supreme Tribunals: A Judiciary without Separate Personnel

The superuniverse has a judicial branch, but it has no separate personnel [15:12.1]. Depending on the case, an Ancient of Days, a Perfector of Wisdom, or a Divine Counselor presides; the Censors present the evidence, the Mighty Messengers defend the children of time, and Those High in Authority voice the attitude of the higher government [15:12.1]. The Sons of the local universes can decree the survival of mortal man, "⟦Q 15:12.2⟧but only the Ancients of Days may sit in executive judgment on the issues of eternal life and death⟦/Q⟧" [15:12.2]. There is no appeal from their verdicts [15:12.4].

5. The Sector Governments and the Trinity Regime

The major sectors, each about one tenth of a superuniverse, are administered by the Perfections of Days, and the minor sectors, each containing about one billion inhabitable worlds, by the Recents of Days [15:13.1, 15:13.4]. The reports of the Unions of Days stationed in the local universes and of the Faithfuls of Days attached to the constellations go up through the minor and major sectors to the courts of the Ancients of Days [15:13.6]. The superuniverses, however, are wholly isolated from one another and know of each other's affairs only through the Paradise clearinghouse [15:10.23].

6. The Shape of the Future

Because the ruling prerogatives of the Ancients of Days were not acquired by experience, they will someday be superseded by the Supreme Being, the experiential sovereign, and will become his vicegerents [18:3.8]. In the present age, while the evolution of the Supreme is incomplete, they are providing a co-ordinated and perfect administrative overcontrol [18:3.9].

Summary

The superuniverse government consists of an executive branch of seven groups headed by the Ancients of Days, a deliberative assembly made up of ascendant graduates, and supreme tribunals that operate without separate personnel [15:10.3-10, 15:11.2, 15:12.1]. The final verdicts concerning eternal life and death are entrusted to them alone [15:12.2, 18:3.7], and this government is the place where perfection and evolution meet face to face and co-operate [15:11.1].

q172.question: What is "virtue" as The Urantia Book speaks of it, and how does man's moral nature differ from animal intelligence?
q172.answer:
The Urantia Book says, "⟦Q 16:7.1⟧A inteligência, por si só, não pode explicar a natureza moral.⟦/Q⟧" [16:7.1]. Morality, virtue, is indigenous to human personality, and moral intuition, the realization of duty, is a component of human mind endowment, together with scientific curiosity and spiritual insight [16:7.1]. What especially distinguishes man from the animal world is not the degree of his intelligence but his moral and religious natures [16:7.1].

And virtue is defined as "⟦Q 16:7.6⟧righteousness—conformity with the cosmos⟦/Q⟧" [16:7.6]. Virtue is known not by naming it but by living it, and it is realized in daily life by consistently choosing good rather than evil [16:7.6].

1. The Animal Learns by Leaping, the Personality by Looking

The selective responses of animals are limited to the motor level of behavior, and the insight of the higher animals ordinarily appears only after motor trial and error [16:7.2]. Man, by contrast, can exercise scientific, moral, and spiritual insight prior to all exploration or experimentation [16:7.2]. "⟦Q 16:7.3⟧A personality can look before it leaps⟦/Q⟧" [16:7.3], and therefore learns not only from leaping but also from looking.

2. Discriminating Not Only Means but Ends

An animal, as experience accumulates, can choose one among several ways of reaching a goal. But a personality can examine the goal itself and judge its worth [16:7.4]. Intelligence alone merely seeks the best means of attaining indiscriminate ends, whereas a moral being discriminates not only between means but also between ends [16:7.4]. Thus one who chooses virtue knows what he is doing and why, where he is going and how he will get there [16:7.4]. Conversely, when a man fails to discriminate the ends of his striving, he functions on the animal level of existence [16:7.5].

3. Virtue Requires the Art of Measurement

The choice between good and evil is influenced not only by the keenness of the moral nature but also by ignorance, immaturity, and delusion [16:7.7]. Because evil may be committed when, through distortion or deception, the lesser is chosen in place of the greater, a sense of proportion and the art of relative evaluation enter into the exercise of virtue [16:7.7]. Without the art of measurement that discerns meanings with precision, the moral nature would be impotent, and without the cosmic insight that brings consciousness of spiritual values, moral choice would be futile [16:7.8].

4. Morality Spreads Not by Compulsion but by Contagion

"⟦Q 16:7.9⟧A moralidade nunca pode ser promovida pela lei nem pela força.⟦/Q⟧" [16:7.9]. It is a personal and freewill matter and must be disseminated by "contagion," through the contact of morally fragrant persons with those who are in some measure desirous of doing the Father's will [16:7.9]. Here lies the reason why a community of faith should value the example of life more than rules.

5. Supreme Virtue

Moral acts are performances of the highest intelligence, guided by discrimination in the choice of superior ends and in the selection of moral means to attain those ends [16:7.10]. Thus the book concludes: "⟦Q 16:7.10⟧A suprema virtude, então, será escolher, de todo o coração, cumprir a vontade do Pai nos céus.⟦/Q⟧" [16:7.10]. The explanation that the relative free will of human personality is concerned with moral decisions and with wholehearted devotion to doing the Father's will is in the same vein [16:8.7-8, 16:8.13].

Summary

Virtue is righteousness, conformity with the cosmos, and it is realized in a life that consistently chooses the good [16:7.6]. The animal learns means through trial and error, but the personality has insight in advance of experience and discerns the value of the ends themselves [16:7.3-4]. Morality spreads not by compulsion but by the contagion of fragrant lives [16:7.9], and its summit is wholeheartedly choosing to do the will of the Father [16:7.10].

q173.question: What does "cosmic discrimination" mean, by which the cosmic mind responds on the three levels of causation, duty, and worship?
q173.answer:
According to The Urantia Book, the Seven Master Spirits are the sevenfold source of the cosmic mind, and the cosmic mind is a subabsolute manifestation of the mind of the Third Source and Center [16:6.1]. Urantians live under the influence of the Creative Spirit of Nebadon rather than the direct influence of the Seven Master Spirits, yet the Master Spirits still dominate the basic reactions of all creature mind [16:6.2]. The ability of this cosmic mind to respond unerringly on three levels of reality, namely causation, duty, and worship, is what the book calls "cosmic discrimination" [16:6.5-8].

Because of this endowment, man is not the helpless victim of the implicit a priori assumptions of science, philosophy, and religion [16:6.4].

1. Reality Response: The Ability of Mind to Respond to Reality

All personality associations of the cosmic mind have a quality that might be called the "reality response" [16:6.4]. Just as energy-matter responds to gravity, the reality sensitivity of the cosmic mind responds to certain phases of reality [16:6.4]. The fact of the cosmic mind also explains the kinship of various types of minds, and this is why human minds sometimes move in channels of agreement that cannot be explained [16:6.3].

2. The Three Cosmic Discriminations

Causation: the reality domain of the physical senses, the scientific realm of logical uniformity, and "⟦Q 16:6.6⟧the mathematical form of the cosmic discrimination⟦/Q⟧" [16:6.6].

Duty: the reality domain of morals in the philosophic realm, the recognition of relative right and wrong; this is the judicial form of the cosmic discrimination [16:6.7].

Worship: the spiritual domain of religious experience, the personal realization of divine fellowship, the assurance of eternal survival. This is "⟦Q 16:6.8⟧the highest insight of the cosmic mind⟦/Q⟧" [16:6.8], the worshipful form of the cosmic discrimination.

3. The Starting Point of Science, Philosophy, and Religion

These three insights are the a priori assumptions that enable man to function as a rational and self-conscious personality in the realms of science, philosophy, and religion [16:6.10]. Matter-energy is recognized by the mathematical logic of the senses; mind-reason intuitively knows its moral duty; spirit-faith recognizes the reality of spiritual experience [16:6.10]. And it is these three cosmic intuitions that give objective validity to human experience of things, meanings, and values [16:6.10]. In the description of Urantia personality, too, the three recognitions of the uniformity of causation, moral duty, and fellowship worship of Deity appear again [16:8.15-18].

4. When Unified, They Make for Strong Character

These three factors may be unified in personality development or may become unbalanced in relation to one another. But when unified, they produce a strong character consisting of a correlation of factual science, moral philosophy, and genuine religious experience [16:6.10]. The book laments that too few persons on Urantia take delight in cultivating the qualities of courageous and independent cosmic thinking [16:6.9].

5. The Purpose of Education, Civilization, and Religion

The book says that it is the purpose of education to develop these endowments, of civilization to express them, of life experience to realize them, "⟦Q 16:6.11⟧of religion to ennoble them; and of personality to unify them⟦/Q⟧" [16:6.11]. The believer should not fear science or regard morality merely as law, but should cultivate the three insights together and so achieve a balanced personality.

Summary

Cosmic discrimination is the threefold recognition of reality possessed by every will creature endowed with the cosmic mind: causation (science), duty (morality), and worship (religion) [16:6.5-9]. It is the a priori foundation of science, philosophy, and religion, and gives objective validity to experience [16:6.10]. When the three are unified, strong character results, and to unify them is the purpose of personality [16:6.10-11].

q174.question: What is "reflectivity," by which the superuniverse headquarters instantly knows what happens in the universe, and who are Majeston and the Reflective Spirits?
q174.answer:
Reflectivity is a marvelous universe phenomenon by which the superuniverse headquarters knows the important happenings within that superuniverse and transmits information upward to the central universe and downward to the local universes [15:10.2]. The Urantia Book says that reflectivity is a phenomenon of the mind levels of the Conjoint Actor, the Supreme Being, and the Master Spirits, and that it is transmissible to the beings concerned in its working [17:3.3]. Yet even the revelators do not fully understand its basic details, and reflectivity is kept on Spiritington as "⟦Q 13:1.10⟧a secret of God the Spirit⟦/Q⟧" [13:1.10].

1. Majeston: The Chief of Reflectivity

When all forty-nine Reflective Spirits had personalized and the cycle of reflective creation was complete, a new and far-reaching reaction occurred in the Deity Absolute, and Majeston, the reflectivity chief, was personalized [17:2.2]. The creation of Majeston was the first supreme creative act of the Supreme Being; the reaction of the Deity Absolute had not been foreseen and far exceeded the intent [17:2.5]. He is a true individual, maintaining Paradise headquarters at the rendezvous of the Seven Master Spirits, and is wholly devoted to the co-ordination and maintenance of the reflectivity service [17:2.3]. Since he is the only personality of divinity created by the Supreme Being in liaison with the Deity Absolute, he is not included in the Paradise personality roll [17:2.4].

2. The Reflective Spirits: Beings Who Reflect the Seven Divine Combinations

The Reflective Spirits are of Trinity origin, forty-nine in all. They were created seven at a time, by the Paradise Trinity in liaison with one of the Seven Master Spirits [17:2.1]. They therefore variously reflect the natures of the seven possible combinations of the divine association of Father, Son, and Spirit, and one of each of the seven types is stationed on each superuniverse headquarters so as to reflect perfectly all manifestations of the three Deities [17:3.1]. The Reflective Spirits of each superuniverse create the Reflective Image Aids, who become their personal voices in the courts of the Ancients of Days [17:3.4].

3. A Living System of Records and News

The Reflective Spirits are not mere transmitting agents but retentive personalities, and everything of true spiritual value is registered in duplicate [17:3.5]. The formal records of the universe are passed up through the angelic recorders, but the true spiritual records are assembled by reflectivity and preserved in the living minds of the family of the Infinite Spirit; "⟦Q 17:3.6⟧These are the live records⟦/Q⟧" [17:3.6]. The reflectivity organization also functions continually as the mechanism for gathering news and promulgating decrees [17:3.7].

4. A Personal, Not Automatic, Operation

Everything of importance that happens at a local universe headquarters is reflected to the superuniverse capital, and conversely, matters of superuniverse importance are reflected to the local universe capitals [17:3.8]. Though it appears to be automatic, it is in reality highly personal and intelligent, and its precision results from the perfection of personality co-operation [17:3.8]. Thus the Ancients of Days need not personally leave their worlds, for those worlds are the superuniverse focal points of the far-flung reflectivity system [18:3.5].

5. Range and Mystery

In the present universe age the range of the reflectivity service appears to be limited to the periphery of the seven superuniverses, but otherwise it seems to be independent of time and space [17:3.10]. Thought Adjusters do not participate in the operation of this system, but there is reason to believe that they are fully cognizant of its transactions and able to avail themselves of them [17:3.9]. Interestingly, neither the Master Spirits nor the Deities themselves directly disclose such powers of reflectivity, yet they created beings who possess them, and the book says: "⟦Q 17:3.3⟧Divine heredity does sometimes disclose in the creature certain attributes which are not discernible in the Creator⟦/Q⟧" [17:3.3].

Summary

Reflectivity is the system by which the superuniverse headquarters knows and transmits the important happenings of the universes above and below and preserves spiritual values as living records [15:10.2, 17:3.5-7]. At its center is Majeston, personalized by the first creative act of the Supreme Being [17:2.2-5], and the forty-nine Reflective Spirits and their aids carry on this work in each superuniverse [17:3.1, 17:3.4]. It is not an automatic device but the result of personal co-operation [17:3.8], and it remains a secret of God the Spirit [13:1.10].

q175.question: What kind of beings are the "Inspired Trinity Spirits," said to be wholly secret, and how are they related to human beings?
q175.answer:
The Inspired Trinity Spirits are one of the few orders of wholly secret beings that have come into existence by the act of the Paradise Trinity [19:5.1]. Even the revelator of Trinity origin who wrote this account confesses that he does not fully understand their nature and conduct, and says that they probably belong to the category of superpersonal spirits [19:5.2]. In a word the book calls them "⟦Q 19:5.3⟧a secret of the Paradise Trinity⟦/Q⟧" [19:5.3].

Nevertheless, the book offers an interesting inference that their activities may not be unrelated to the spiritual growth of us human beings.

1. Origin and Nature

They come into existence by the act of the Trinity, and they may be utilized by one, two, or all three of the Deities [19:5.1]. It is not known whether their number is complete or increasing, but the revelator believes it is not fixed [19:5.1]. They function through all known circuits and appear to act almost independently of time and space [19:5.2]. They are not a part of the revealed organization that conducts the time-space universes before light and life, and they have no clearly discernible place in the administration of the superuniverses [19:5.3].

2. Who Can Recognize Them?

Under certain conditions they can individualize themselves sufficiently to be recognized by beings of Trinity origin, but the lower orders of celestial beings can never recognize them [19:5.3]. Much of what is known about them comes from the Solitary Messengers, who detect the nearness of these Spirits as the magnetic needle points to the magnetic pole [19:5.5]. The revelator writes that even at the moment of writing, an associate Solitary Messenger informs him that a Spirit of this order is present with them, within twenty-five feet [19:5.7].

3. A Possible Connection with Thought Adjusters

When a Solitary Messenger is on a planet whose inhabitants are indwelt by Thought Adjusters, as on Urantia, a qualitative excitation occurs in his sensitivity of spirit-presence detection [19:5.6]. In contact with the natives of planets that do not receive Adjusters there is no such response. This suggests that the Thought Adjusters are in some way associated with the Inspired Spirits, but the revelator says he does not really know [19:5.6]. Since Adjusters originate in the Father alone and Inspired Spirits in the Trinity, the two are not of the same order [19:5.6].

4. Possibly Superconscious Teachers

The revelator's most interesting conclusion is this: just as the Trinity Teacher Sons are devoted to the conscious enlightenment of universe creatures, the Inspired Trinity Spirits, "⟦Q 19:5.9⟧by superconscious techniques, are also functioning as teachers of the realms⟦/Q⟧" [19:5.9]. There is a body of spiritual knowledge essential to high spiritual attainment that cannot be consciously received, and self-consciousness might actually jeopardize its reception [19:5.9]. The Sons of God, too, are not conscious of the counsel of the Inspired Spirits, yet they tell of happenings that are difficult to explain without taking the activity of such Spirits into account [19:5.10].

5. Their Future Role

The Melchizedeks of Nebadon teach that the Inspired Trinity Spirits are destined, in the eternal future, to function in the place of the Solitary Messengers, whose number is slowly diminishing [19:5.4].

6. The Lesson for Us

The revelator says he does not believe they are playing hide and seek, and that he is satisfied "⟦Q 19:5.11⟧that there are no arbitrary secrets in the universe⟦/Q⟧" [19:5.11]. And he counsels that we mortals have a long way to go before we can depend on the assurance of sight, so that for a long time we shall make use of faith and depend on revelation if we are to progress rapidly and safely [19:5.12]. Not being conscious of unseen help does not mean that the help is absent.

Summary

The Inspired Trinity Spirits are superpersonal and wholly secret spirits of Trinity origin, whose presence only the Solitary Messengers can sense [19:5.1-5]. They may have a special connection with worlds indwelt by Adjusters [19:5.6], and they may be teachers who superconsciously impart spiritual truth that cannot be received consciously [19:5.9]. This mystery reminds us that we must advance relying on faith and revelation rather than on what is seen [19:5.12].

q176.question: How is the mortal bestowal of an Avonal Son like, and how is it unlike, the bestowal of a Michael (a Creator Son)?
q176.answer:
The Urantia Book says: "⟦Q 20:6.5⟧As carreiras de auto-outorga mortal dos Michaéis e Avonais, ainda que equiparáveis, não são idênticas em todos os aspectos: um Filho Magisterial nunca proclama “Quem tiver visto o Filho, terá visto o Pai”, como o fez o vosso Filho Criador, quando em Urântia vivendo na carne.⟦/Q⟧" [20:6.5]. Both Sons are born of woman, grow up as human beings, pass through death, and open the way for the outpouring of the Spirit of Truth. But the will that is the source of the bestowal, the number and form of the bestowals, and their meaning within the universe differ.

It should first be made clear that the purpose of a bestowal is not to change the attitude of the Father. The bestowals of the Avonals and the Michaels are an essential part of the experiential training that makes these Sons safe and sympathetic magistrates and rulers of the peoples of time and space [20:5.2].

1. The Likeness: A Truly Human Life

On a mortal-bestowal mission a Paradise Son is always born of woman, grows up through infancy and youth to manhood, and becomes in every way like the human beings of his race [20:6.2]. There is, however, the universal restriction that he does not leave offspring on the bestowal world [20:6.2]. He toils in various callings [20:6.3], and after achieving perfect harmony with the indwelling Thought Adjuster, he begins his mission as a teacher who awakens the minds of his brethren [20:6.4]. Both, upon entering the portals of death, reappear on the third day [20:6.6].

2. The Difference: By Whose Will He Comes

Michael on Urantia proclaimed that whoever has seen the Son has seen the Father, but an Avonal never so proclaims. Instead, he declares: "⟦Q 20:6.5⟧Whosoever has seen me has seen the Eternal Son of God⟦/Q⟧" [20:6.5]. The Avonals are not of immediate descent from the Father and do not incarnate subject to the Father's will; always do they bestow themselves subject to the will of the Eternal Son [20:6.5].

3. The Difference: Once and Seven Times

An Avonal bestowal is always in the likeness of mortal flesh, whereas the seven bestowals of a Creator Son include appearing on seven creature levels of being [21:4.2]. Only once in his sevenfold bestowal career is a Michael born of woman, and only once does he live and die as a member of the lowest order of evolutionary will creatures [21:4.3]. Most inhabited worlds receive an Avonal bestowal Son; the one exception is the single planet chosen by the Creator Son for his mortal bestowal [20:5.4].

4. Their Effectiveness Is Not Different

Of the planetary services of the Avonals the book emphasizes: "⟦Q 20:5.6⟧in no way are these planetary services inferior to the mortal bestowals of the Michaels⟦/Q⟧" [20:5.6]. No planet could ever be in such a condition that it would require the bestowal of a Creator Son for its spiritual rehabilitation; any Son of the bestowal group would have equally sufficed [20:5.6]. Moreover, there is no record of failure by an Avonal or a Michael on a bestowal mission [20:5.7].

5. Death and the Spirit of Truth

A bestowal Son must encounter death, but it is not a requirement of the divine plan that this death be violent [20:6.6]. Most planets afford a more considerate reception, and Urantia, because of the unusually cruel experience through which Jesus passed, has become known as "⟦Q 20:6.6⟧the world of the cross⟦/Q⟧" [20:6.6]. A bestowal Son lays down his life voluntarily, not to appease stern justice or divine wrath, but to complete his bestowal [20:6.7]. After an Avonal bestowal, the conjoint Spirit of Truth of that Son and the Creator Son is sent [20:6.8], and when the final bestowal of a Michael is completed, that Spirit becomes more literally the spirit of the sovereign Michael [20:6.9]. It is also after the outpouring of this Spirit of Truth that Adjusters come to all normal human beings [20:5.3].

Summary

Avonals and Michaels are both born, live, and die as true human beings, and they open the way of the Spirit of Truth [20:6.2, 20:6.6, 20:6.8]. But an Avonal bestows himself once by the will of the Eternal Son and reveals the Eternal Son, whereas a Michael bestows himself on seven creature levels and at last reveals the Father [20:6.5, 21:4.2-3]. Their effectiveness is not different [20:5.6], and Urantia receives special attention because it was the stage of Michael's final bestowal [20:5.5].

q177.question: When a Creator Son creates a local universe, what can he make by himself, and in what matters does he need the consent or co-operation of the other Deities?
q177.answer:
A Creator Son is the designer, creator, builder, and administrator of a local universe [21:2.1]. He leaves Paradise and becomes the head of his universe, to all practical purposes its God [21:2.2], but his creative prerogatives are not unlimited. The Urantia Book explains that his departure liberates his creator prerogatives from the Paradise sources, yet he remains subject to certain limitations inherent in the pre-existence of those sources [21:2.3].

1. A Long Preparation before Creation

A Creator Son may choose the space site of his universe, but before beginning its physical organization he must spend a long period of observation, studying the efforts of his older brothers who created universes earlier in the same superuniverse [21:2.1]. Before this he completes the long and unique experience of Paradise observation and Havona training [21:2.1]. The Creator Son is accompanied by a creative daughter of the Infinite Spirit, the one who is to become the divine minister, the Mother Spirit, of the new local universe [21:2.2].

2. Three Limitations of Creative Prerogative

Energy-matter: this is dominated by the Infinite Spirit. Before a Creator Son can create any new form of things or attempt any new transmutation of energy-matter, he must secure the consent and working co-operation of the Infinite Spirit [21:2.4].

Creature designs and types: these are controlled by the Eternal Son. Before making any new type of being or new design of creature, the Creator Son must secure the consent of the Eternal Son [21:2.5].

Personality: "⟦Q 21:2.6⟧A personalidade é projetada e outorgada pelo Pai Universal.⟦/Q⟧" [21:2.6]. The Creator Son cannot bestow personality by himself.

Furthermore, the types and patterns of mind are determined by precreature factors, and after a creature has been constituted, mind is bestowed by the Third Source and Center [21:2.7]. Spirit design is finally controlled by the spirit endowment of the Trinity or of the Trinity personalities [21:2.8].

3. Co-creation with the Mother Spirit

When the problems of universe materialization and equilibrium have been settled and the Creator Son has formed a co-operative working union with the complemental Daughter of the Infinite Spirit, the two begin the liaison that gives origin to the numerous hosts of local universe children [21:2.9]. At this time the creative Spirit focalization of the Infinite Spirit changes in nature, taking on the personal qualities of the local universe Mother Spirit [21:2.9]. Thus the native beings of a local universe inherit half their attributes from the Creative Spirits, who are similar, and the other half from the Creator Sons, who differ from one another [21:2.10].

4. The Source of Diversity

All Creator Sons resemble their Paradise parents, yet none exactly resembles another; each is unique in both personality and nature [21:2.10]. Because of this diversity the life forms of the realms they found are also diverse, and no two realms are inhabited by native beings identical in every respect [21:2.10].

5. The Universe Goes On Even When the Son Is Absent

When a Creator Son is absent, the government is directed by the first-born native being, the Bright and Morning Star, and the Mother Spirit always remains at headquarters, carrying on her spiritual ministry [21:2.11]. Even when the Son lays down the lines of power in order to incarnate as a child of time, his realm continues to swing on, for no material organization is independent of the absolute gravity of Paradise and the overcontrol of the Unqualified Absolute [21:2.12]. This is also the background that made it possible for Michael to live as Jesus.

6. The Change after Sovereignty Is Attained

When he has completed his seven bestowals and attained supreme sovereignty, the power to create wholly new types of creatures in the present universe age passes from the Michael Son [21:5.6]. But the work of life elaboration already begun continues without interruption [21:5.6].

Summary

The Creator Son designs and builds the local universe, but in energy-matter he must have the consent and co-operation of the Infinite Spirit, and in creature design that of the Eternal Son, while personality is bestowed by the Universal Father alone [21:2.4-6]. Mind is bestowed by the Third Source, and spirit design is controlled by the Trinity [21:2.7-8]. He brings forth children together with the Mother Spirit [21:2.9], and because of his unique individuality, life is richly varied in each local universe [21:2.10].

q178.question: A Creator Son could have possessed full sovereignty from the beginning, so why does he earn his sovereignty "by experience" through seven bestowals?
q178.answer:
The Urantia Book says: "⟦Q 21:3.3⟧The fact of creatorship implies the fullness of sovereignty, but the Michaels choose to experientially earn it⟦/Q⟧" [21:3.3]. A Creator Son is at first given his universe with the consent of the Trinity and the confirmation of the Master Spirit, but this is only a kind of cosmic leasehold [21:3.1]. His elevation to the experiential supremacy of sovereignty comes as the result of the personal experience accumulated in the work of universe creation and incarnated bestowals [21:3.1]. Until then he rules as the vicegerent of the Universal Father [21:3.1].

1. Why He Does Not Assert Sovereignty in Advance

A Creator Son could at any time assert full sovereignty, but he wisely chooses not to [21:3.2]. If he were to assume unearned supreme sovereignty before passing through the bestowals, the Paradise personalities in his local universe would withdraw [21:3.2]. By earning sovereignty experientially, the Michaels retain the full co-operation of all Paradise personalities [21:3.3]. He swears to the Trinity that he will not assume supreme sovereignty until his seven bestowals are completed and certified by the superuniverse rulers, and such an oath would have no meaning if he did not have the power to do so [21:3.12]. This, in other words, is the voluntary humility of a freewill Son [21:3.3].

2. The Stages of Sovereignty

The book says that sovereignty passes through six, possibly seven, stages: initial vicegerent sovereignty, joint vicegerent sovereignty, augmenting vicegerent sovereignty, supreme sovereignty, increased supreme sovereignty, Trinitarian sovereignty, and unrevealed sovereignty [21:3.4-11]. In Nebadon, supreme sovereignty began with the end of Michael's Urantia bestowal and has existed for a little over nineteen hundred years [21:3.8].

3. The Content of the Seven Bestowals

The seven bestowals include appearing on seven creature levels of being and are related to the seven primary expressions of the will and nature of Deity [21:4.2]. Their technique includes experientially penetrating the seven levels in the very likeness of the creatures, dedicating himself to each phase of the sevenfold will of Deity as it is personalized in the Seven Master Spirits, and unifying these two experiences [21:3.17-22]. Their repercussions augment the sovereignty of the Supreme Being and factualize Michael's supreme local universe sovereignty [21:3.23]. After each bestowal he goes to the "⟦Q 21:4.4⟧right hand of the Father⟦/Q⟧" to gain acceptance [21:4.4].

4. Jesus' "It Is Finished"

The divine Son who appeared on Urantia was a Creator Son who had already completed six phases [21:4.5]. Therefore, when he gave up the life of the flesh, he could truly say "It is finished," and that death was the last step that completed his bestowal career [21:4.5]. From then on he rules no longer as a vicegerent but in his own right and name as "⟦Q 21:4.5⟧King of Kings and Lord of Lords⟦/Q⟧" [21:4.5].

5. A Way of Revealing the Nature of God

In the course of settling the question of sovereignty, the Creator Son not only demonstrates his fitness to rule but also reveals the nature of the Paradise Deities [21:3.24]. He humbles himself to take on the form and experience of the creature, and becomes the true revealer of the Father's loving nature and gracious authority [21:3.24]. A Creator who has completed his bestowals adds the experience of the creature to his nature and rises to the experiential plane of a "Master Son" [21:4.6].

6. A Comfort for Us

The book says that even the Gods must pass through an equivalent experience before they are accounted experientially competent to rule their universes fully; so "⟦Q 21:4.6⟧Why should man bemoan his lowly origin and enforced evolutionary career⟦/Q⟧" [21:4.6]! Growth through experience is the path that even the Sons of God walk.

Summary

A Creator Son could have asserted sovereignty from the beginning, but he chooses to earn it by experience through bestowals on seven creature levels [21:3.2-3, 21:4.2]. In this way he retains the co-operation of all Paradise personalities, reveals the sevenfold will and nature of Deity, and becomes a sympathetic ruler [21:3.3, 21:3.24]. Jesus' "It is finished" was the completion of this very seventh bestowal [21:4.5].

q179.question: What relationship does Michael, the Master Son who has completed his seven bestowals, have with his universe, and what is his future destiny?
q179.answer:
When a Creator Son completes his seven bestowals, he is reckoned as a separate order, a sevenfold Master Son [21:4.6]. The Urantia Book says that the power of a Master Michael is unlimited because it is derived from experienced association with the Trinity, and unquestioned because it is derived from actual experience as the very creatures subject to that authority [21:5.1]. Concerning his future, no one can speak with final authority, but the revelators infer that he will go on to service transcending the finite [21:6.1-2].

1. Three Reasons Why His Sovereignty Is Supreme

The sovereignty of a sevenfold Creator Son is supreme because it embraces the sevenfold viewpoint of Paradise Deity, because it embodies the sevenfold attitude of time-space creatures, and because it perfectly synthesizes the two [21:5.1-4]. This sovereignty therefore encompasses all the divinity of God the Sevenfold, culminating in the Supreme Being, and is like the future sovereignty of the Supreme Being that will someday be completed [21:5.5].

2. New Creation Ceases, and the Work of Nurture Begins

When supreme sovereignty is attained, the power to create wholly new types of creatures in the present universe age passes from Michael [21:5.6]. But the work of life elaboration already established continues without interruption, and the Master Son becomes responsible for personal devotion to the fostering and administering of what has already been created [21:5.6]. The book calls this the beginning of settled administration in a local universe [21:5.6].

3. The End of Confusion and the Triumph of Justice

The elevation of a Master Son means the beginning of the end of agelong uncertainty and confusion [21:5.7]. Thereafter, that which cannot be spiritualized will eventually be disorganized, and that which cannot be co-ordinated with cosmic reality will eventually be destroyed [21:5.7]. After endless mercy and patience have been fully extended, "⟦Q 21:5.7⟧Aquilo que a misericórdia não puder reabilitar, a justiça finalmente irá aniquilar.⟦/Q⟧" [21:5.7].

4. A Ruler Supreme in His Own Universe

Once settled, the Master Michaels are supreme in authority, responsibility, and administrative power in their local universes, and there is no insight that surpasses their wisdom concerning the functioning of their universe [21:5.8]. He controls all other Sons of God in his domain and may modify the procedures of spiritual adjudication and evolutionary adjustment on the inhabited planets [21:5.9]. Especially with regard to the world of his creature sojourn and the planet of his incarnation in mortal flesh, he makes and carries out plans of his own choosing [21:5.9].

5. Intimate Contact through the Spirit of Truth

The Master Sons seem to be in perfect communication not only with the worlds of their own sojourn but with all worlds on which a Magisterial Son has bestowed himself, and this contact is maintained by their spiritual presence, the Spirit of Truth [21:5.10]. They possess "⟦Q 21:5.10⟧a sympathetic reach which extends from the Universal Father on high to the lowly races of planetary life in the realms of time⟦/Q⟧" [21:5.10]. Here lies the ground on which we can commune with Jesus through the Spirit of Truth.

6. Future Destiny: The Way, the Truth, and the Life

The revelators believe that each Michael is the absolute of the dual-deity concepts of his origin and embodies actual phases of the infinity of the Father and the Son [21:6.1]. The completion of the bestowal career signifies the appearance of a capacity for service transcending the finite, and they see the restriction on creating new creatures as made necessary by the liberation of these superfinite potentials [21:6.2]. In the far future, in the universes of outer space, the union of a Master Son and a seventh-stage Creative Spirit may attain to service on subabsolute levels [21:6.3]. And the revelators believe that in eternity the Michaels are literally destined to be "⟦Q 21:6.4⟧the way, the truth, and the life⟦/Q⟧," lighting the path for all universe personalities [21:6.4].

Summary

Master Michael rules his universe with a supreme sovereignty that synthesizes the viewpoint of Deity and the experience of the creature [21:5.1-5]; instead of new creation he fosters the life that already exists and communicates with all his worlds through the Spirit of Truth [21:5.6, 21:5.10]. Under his rule, justice prevails after mercy has been exhausted [21:5.7]. His future is service beyond the finite, to be forever the way, the truth, and the life of all personalities [21:6.2-4].

q180.question: What does the story of the Celestial Guardians and High Son Assistants, trinitized without experience, envying ascending mortals teach us?
q180.answer:
The Celestial Guardians and High Son Assistants are creature-trinitized sons: offspring trinitized by perfected humans and by Paradise-Havona personalities, who were then embraced by the Paradise Trinity [22:9.1]. Because they have not personally passed through the ascending career, they are marvelous beings and yet deficient in experience [22:9.6]. The Mighty Messenger who tells this story says that, seeing them look so longingly even at those newly arrived on the mansion worlds, he could not help realizing that they really envied their supposedly less fortunate brethren who walk the path of experience [22:9.8].

This passage shows how precious "actual experience" is in the universe, and teaches us to be grateful for our lowly origin.

1. Who They Are and How They Are Assigned

The creature-trinitized sons are embraced by the Trinity in groups of seven thousand, and they are assigned to the superuniverses on the recommendation of their former teachers, the Trinity Teacher Sons [22:9.1]. Those who have shown more satisfactory service become High Son Assistants, and those less distinguished become Celestial Guardians [22:9.1]. They are versed in the affairs of the ascending career, not by having ascended themselves, but as a result of serving with the Trinity Teacher Sons [22:9.2].

2. The Celestial Guardians: Officers of the Superuniverse Courts

There are almost one billion Celestial Guardians in Orvonton, assigned chiefly to the major sector headquarters [22:9.3]. As officers of the courts of the Ancients of Days they function as court messengers and bearers of summons and decisions, and they are the apprehending agents who bring in the beings required to appear before the superuniverse judges [22:9.4]. They have never been indwelt by Adjusters, nor are they Spirit fused or Son fused, but the embrace of the Trinity compensates for their nonfused status [22:9.5].

3. The High Son Assistants: Ideas Personified

The High Son Assistants are the personality embodiment of some divine idea, some universal ideal, as it has never before been conceived or trinitized [22:10.2]. The book says, "⟦Q 22:10.2⟧Eles são aquela idéia personificada.⟦/Q⟧" [22:10.2]. Therefore, in dealing with problems concerning that idea, they are inexpressibly useful, and the revelator recalls how keenly he realized their value in the work of commissions [22:10.4]. They are touchingly affectionate and loyal, supremely wise concerning their one idea, yet humble beings who seek knowledge in other fields even from ascending mortals [22:10.8].

4. Nothing Takes the Place of Experience

Their limitation lies in the fact that their experiential capacity is time-space inhibited [22:9.7]. The book declares: "⟦Q 22:9.7⟧There is simply nothing in all universal existence which can take the place of actual personal experience⟦/Q⟧" [22:9.7]. They are held in reserve for experiential function in a future universe age [22:9.7]. Thus they are neither as versatile nor as dependable as the ascenders, and they lack the profound personal experience of those who have climbed up to glory from the dark domains of space [22:9.6].

5. Gratitude for Our Origin

The revelator, who has an ascending career, confesses that they love these beings and try to compensate their deficiencies, "⟦Q 22:9.6⟧but they make us ever grateful for our lowly origin and our capacity for experience⟦/Q⟧" [22:9.6]. Their willingness to acknowledge their deficiencies is said to be transcendently beautiful and sometimes most touchingly pathetic [22:9.6]. The trials and struggles we pass through now are precious assets that other beings envy.

6. We Too Can Take Part in Trinitization

Because the High Son Assistants are so valuable in superuniverse administration, Uversa encourages the pilgrims of space and the Paradise residents to attempt trinitization after they have contributed to each other the needed experience [22:10.6]. The experience of today may become the groundwork from which a new being is brought forth in the distant future.

Summary

The Celestial Guardians and High Son Assistants are creature-trinitized sons embraced by the Trinity who serve preciously in the superuniverse government but lack the actual experience of ascension [22:9.1-6, 22:10.1-2]. Therefore they envy the mortals who walk the path of experience [22:9.8], and from them we learn the truth that nothing takes the place of experience, and the reason to be grateful for our lowly origin [22:9.6-7].

q181.question: What are the Census Directors, and how do they record a person's birth and death?
q181.answer:
The Census Directors are a special and completed creation of the Infinite Spirit, charged with keeping count of all will creatures in the universe [24:2.2]. Although the cosmic mind already knows of the existence and whereabouts of every thinking creature, there operates in the universe of universes a separate, independent technique for counting all will creatures [24:2.1]. They were created to be in perfect synchrony with the reflectivity technique of the superuniverses, and at the same time they are personally sensitive and responsive to intelligent will [24:2.2].

The key point is that what the Census Directors record is not "the birth and death of the body" but "the appearance and the last exercise of will."

1. They Know the Instant Will Appears

By a technique not wholly understood, the Census Directors are aware of the birth of will anywhere in the grand universe the instant it occurs [24:2.2]. They are therefore always competent to report at once the number, nature, and whereabouts of the will creatures in any part of the central creation and the seven superuniverses [24:2.2]. They do not, however, function on Paradise, for there knowledge is inherent and the Deities know all [24:2.2].

2. The First and the Last Act of Will

"⟦Q 24:2.8⟧Os Diretores do Censo registram a existência de uma nova criatura de vontade sempre que acontece o primeiro ato de vontade; indicam a morte de uma criatura de vontade quando acontece o seu último ato de vontade.⟦/Q⟧" [24:2.8]. The partial emergence of will seen in certain of the higher animals does not belong to their domain; they keep count of nothing but bona fide will creatures [24:2.8]. Exactly how they register the function of will, even the revelator does not know [24:2.8]. This illustrates well the view of The Urantia Book that the essence of being human lies in will, the capacity to choose.

3. Organization: From Havona to the Local Universes

Seven Census Directors are stationed one on the pilot world of each Havona circuit, and all the other directors operate under the jurisdiction of the Ancients of Days [24:2.3]. One director presides at each superuniverse headquarters, and under him numerous directors are stationed at the capital of each local universe [24:2.4]. In Orvonton, the seventh superuniverse, there are one hundred thousand Census Directors available for assignment to the local universes [24:2.5]. Usatia, the chief of Orvonton, does not register intelligent will directly but functions as the tabulating personality who compiles the reports coming in from each local creation [24:2.5]. These census data belong to the superuniverse and are not transmitted to Havona or Paradise [24:2.6].

4. Counters, Not Recorders

The Census Directors are concerned with human beings only to the extent of recording the fact of will function [24:2.7]. They are not concerned with the records of a person's life and doings, and they are not in any sense recording personalities [24:2.7]. There is therefore no need to mistake them for beings who keep watch over our conduct.

5. One Who Knows Me at This Very Moment

The book tells us a remarkable fact. The Census Director of Nebadon, now stationed on Salvington, "⟦Q 24:2.7⟧is at this very moment personally conscious and aware of your living presence here on Urantia⟦/Q⟧" [24:2.7], and the moment we cease to function as will creatures he will at once afford the records confirmation of our death [24:2.7]. It is a comfort that in so vast a universe one person's existence is known in such a personal way.

6. Infallible Individuals

These beings have always been Census Directors and always will be; they are relatively useless for other work, but in their own function they are infallible [24:2.9]. They are never negligent and they never falsify, and despite their marvelous powers they are individuals with recognizable spirit presence and form [24:2.9].

Summary

The Census Directors are beings created by the Infinite Spirit who, synchronized with reflectivity, know the number, nature, and whereabouts of all will creatures in the universe [24:2.2]. They register a person's existence at the first act of will and record his death at the last act of will [24:2.8], but they do not record his doings [24:2.7]. Even now the Census Director of Nebadon knows the living presence of each one of us [24:2.7].

q182.question: Who are the Graduate Guides who lead ascenders in Havona, and how did they come into being?
q182.answer:
The Graduate Guides are among the higher personalities of the Infinite Spirit, devoted to the task of piloting the mortal graduates from the superuniverses of time through the Havona course of education and training [24:6.1]. They conduct the high university of technical instruction and spiritual training that mortals need in order to reach the goal of the ages, God, rest, and the eternity of perfected service, and they prepare the ascending pilgrims to enter Paradise and the Corps of the Finality [24:6.1].

Their origin is something of a mystery, but the revelators believe that they are transformed beings who were formerly experienced members of the Havona Servitals [24:6.4, 24:7.1].

1. A Guide Who Accompanies You throughout Havona

The guide who greets us upon our arrival on the receiving world of the outer Havona circuit will be with us throughout our career on the heavenly circuits [24:6.3]. He follows us to the end of the Havona course and witnesses our falling into the last sleep of time, the transit to Paradise [24:6.3]. When we awaken from that sleep, a Paradise Companion greets us [24:6.3]. The Graduate Guides never leave the Havona worlds, and unless we reject the plan, we shall someday meet these noble beings face to face [24:6.9].

2. The First Guide, Malvorian, and the First Pilgrim, Grandfanda

There was no record of a Graduate Guide until the day when the first mortal pilgrim reached the outer belt of the central creation [24:6.4]. The instant that first pilgrim arrived on the pilot world of the outer circuit, he met Malvorian, the first of the Graduate Guides, who is now the chief of their supreme council [24:6.4]. The name of this pilgrim discoverer of Havona is Grandfanda, and his arrival was the signal for the establishment of the broadcast service of the universe of universes [24:6.8]. When the first pilgrim arrived, "⟦Q 24:6.7⟧the thrill of all time swept through the heavenly courts⟦/Q⟧" [24:6.7].

3. From Havona Servitals to Graduate Guides

Evolution is not the order of the central universe, yet the revelators believe that the Graduate Guides are the perfected or experienced members of the Havona Servitals [24:7.1]. This is because their broad sympathy and their ability to understand ascending creatures appear to have been gained by actual service in the superuniverses [24:7.1]. It happens that an experienced servital, returning from a superuniverse assignment, has personal contact with the central Paradise radiance, is embraced, and is never seen again [24:7.2]. Then, within exactly three moments, a little less than three days of our time, a newly born Graduate Guide appears on the outer circuit of Havona, and their number is exactly equal to the number of servitals who have disappeared [24:7.6]. The special attachment the two orders have for each other also supports this inference [24:7.7].

4. The Participation of the Supreme Being

The Havona Servitals are created by the Seven Master Spirits in co-operation with the Supreme Power Directors, and so they inherently relate to phases of Supremacy [24:7.8]. The revelators believe that this transformation occurs in response to the will of the Infinite Spirit acting for the Supreme, and they surmise that, although the Supreme Being does not create the Graduate Guides, he participates in some way [24:7.8]. With the arrival of the mortal ascenders, extensive modifications began in the organization of the central universe, and the appearance of the Graduate Guides is an act of God the Supreme signifying those modifications [24:7.9].

5. What It Means for Us
