The revelator says that the activities of the Graduate Guides are so superspiritual that they are difficult to portray to the material mind, but that we shall understand them when our vision is enlarged on the mansion worlds, and that the range of our spiritual understanding is not destined always to be so limited [24:6.2]. The fact that even the perfect central universe brought forth new beings in order to receive the children of time shows how great a meaning our ascension has for the whole universe.

Summary

The Graduate Guides are beings who instruct and accompany ascending mortals throughout the seven circuits of Havona [24:6.1, 24:6.3]. They first appeared, with Malvorian, when the first pilgrim, Grandfanda, arrived [24:6.4, 24:6.8], and they are regarded as experienced Havona Servitals transformed through the divine embrace [24:7.1-6]. Their appearance was the Supreme Being's response for the reception of evolutionary creatures [24:7.9].

q183.question: What kind of beings are the "Universal Conciliators," said to settle disputes between worlds, and how do they work?
q183.answer:
The Universal Conciliators are beings created in each superuniverse: each time a Havona Servital is created, one Conciliator comes into being in each superuniverse, seven in all [25:2.1]. When a Master Spirit, in union with the Power Directors, creates a Havona Servital, there is a focalization in one of the Reflective Spirits of each superuniverse, and an equal number of Conciliators appear in full-fledged form at the headquarters of that superuniverse [25:2.2]. They serve as traveling courts that promptly adjudicate the minor difficulties of the universe of universes so that it may run in an orderly manner [25:2.11].

1. A Conciliating Commission of Four in One

The Conciliators are inherently divided into groups of four, three of them spiritual personalities and one a semimaterial being [25:2.5]. The group consists of a judge-arbiter, a spirit-advocate, a divine executioner, and a recorder [25:2.6-9]. The judge-arbiter is designated by the unanimous vote of the other three; the spirit-advocate protects the rights of all persons concerned and presents the evidence; the divine executioner makes contact with material beings and carries out the decisions; and the recorder makes all the records [25:2.6-9]. While court is in session, the spirit-advocate drops out and three function, and so they are also called "referee trios" [25:2.10].

2. They Do Not Deal with Eternal Issues

The Conciliators traverse space at three times the speed of seraphim, and without such commissions the tribunals of the worlds would be hopelessly congested with minor misunderstandings [25:2.11]. But "⟦Q 25:2.12⟧These referee trios do not pass upon matters of eternal import⟦/Q⟧" [25:2.12]. The soul and eternal prospects of a creature of time are never placed in jeopardy by their decisions [25:2.12]. Once a commission has accepted jurisdiction, its rulings are final and unanimous, and there is no appeal [25:2.12].

3. Seven Stages of Service, from the Worlds to the Superuniverse

The Conciliators begin as conciliators to the worlds and are promoted to serve as conciliators to the system headquarters, the constellations, the local universes, the superuniverse minor sectors, the major sectors, and the superuniverse [25:3.3-13]. The young and less experienced commissions begin their service on lowly worlds such as Urantia [25:3.1]. On a world, when one person from each of the contending parties files a petition, the commission functions at once [25:3.3], and it makes no decision until all the evidence has been heard [25:3.4]. The divine executioners are "⟦Q 25:3.5⟧masterful manipulators of that which is in the interests of that which ought to be⟦/Q⟧" [25:3.5], and they sometimes act in strange ways without defying natural law.

4. From Judges to Teachers

As they go to higher levels, their task changes. There is less and less misunderstanding to arbitrate and more and more mysterious phenomena to interpret and explain, so that they evolve from arbiters of differences to explainers of mysteries, from judges to interpretative teachers [25:3.12]. The book says: "⟦Q 25:3.12⟧Quanto mais elevada é a educação de uma criatura, mais respeito ela terá pelo conhecimento, pela experiência e opiniões dos outros.⟦/Q⟧" [25:3.12]. At the superuniverse stage, the divine executioner loses his punitive powers and becomes the physical voice of the spirit trio [25:3.13].

5. Why Conciliation Is Needed in the Universe

The moment the Creators create evolutionary beings with the power of choice, misunderstandings are certain to arise, and provision is needed for the fair adjustment of honest differences of opinion [25:3.7]. The Creators could have made the local universes as perfect as Havona, but they did not; they made universes rich in differences and difficulties, and at the same time provided the means for harmonizing them [25:3.7]. The conflicts in our own lives are likewise part of a universe design for growth, and to seek fair conciliation is to follow the way of the universe.

6. Four Who Are Together Forever

The members of a conciliating commission are never separated; they serve together forever just as they were originally associated [25:3.17]. "⟦Q 25:3.17⟧Eles ficam eternamente associados como uma corporificação da justiça suprema do tempo e do espaço.⟦/Q⟧" [25:3.17]. Not one Conciliator has ever gone astray; they are not infallible in judgment, but they are infallible in faithfulness [25:3.2].

Summary

The Universal Conciliators are beings who come into existence in each superuniverse along with the creation of the Havona Servitals, and four of them, a judge-arbiter, a spirit-advocate, a divine executioner, and a recorder, form one commission [25:2.1-9]. They adjudicate the disputes of time, not of eternal destiny, promptly and fairly [25:2.11-12], and as they rise from the worlds to the superuniverse they grow from judges into teachers [25:3.3-13]. Their existence shows the wisdom of the Creators, who would harmonize the differences that free will brings forth [25:3.7].

q184.question: What kind of beings are the Morontia Companions and the Paradise Companions who receive us on the ascending journey, and what do they do?
q184.answer:
The Urantia Book says that the ascending journey does not consist only of study and testing, but that a ministry of friendship and companionship is provided all along the way. The chief examples are the Morontia Companions of the local universe and the Paradise Companions of Paradise. The Morontia Companions are offspring of the local universe Mother Spirits and are the friends and associates of all who live the morontia life [25:7.1], while the Paradise Companions are beings chosen from the angelic hosts to become personality associates of ascenders on Paradise [25:8.1, 25:8.3].

Neither kind of companion is charged with work essential to ascension, yet for that very reason they reveal the thoughtful love of God.

1. The Morontia Companions: Friends in the Local Universe

The Morontia Companions are not indispensable to the actual progress of the ascenders, nor do they take the place of the seraphic guardians who accompany mortals on the Paradise journey [25:7.1]. They provide gracious hospitality to those who are just beginning the long ascent, and they are excellent sponsors of play, assisted by the reversion directors [25:7.1]. Since they serve only in the local universe, when we finish the morontia career and depart for the superuniverse we will truly regret that they cannot accompany us [25:7.3].

2. Rest and Play Are Also Part of the Ascent

The book says that on the morontia training worlds we must carry on serious and increasingly difficult tasks, but that there will always be opportunities for regular rest and reversion [25:7.2]. Throughout the whole journey toward Paradise there are times of rest and spirit play, and even in the career of light and life there is always time for worship and for new achievements [25:7.2]. The spiritual life includes not only tension and effort but also rest and joy.

3. The Paradise Companions: Beings Who Exist Only to Be With Us

The Paradise Companions are chosen from among the seraphim, seconaphim, supernaphim, and omniaphim [25:8.1]; they are nominated by the local universe Mother Spirits, the superuniverse Reflective Spirits, and Majeston of Paradise, and commissioned by one of the Seven Master Spirits [25:8.2]. Except for permanent status, this service is the highest honor conferred on ministering spirits [25:8.2]. They have nothing especial to accomplish on behalf of those with whom they fraternize; "⟦Q 25:8.3⟧they are simply companions⟦/Q⟧" [25:8.3]. Almost every other being on Paradise will have something to do for us, but these are assigned only to be with us and to commune with us as personality associates [25:8.3].

4. "Not Good for Man to Be Alone"

Mortals come from races that are very social, and because the Creators well know that it is "⟦Q 25:8.4⟧not good for man to be alone⟦/Q⟧," provision is made for companionship even on Paradise [25:8.4]. If we arrive together with a close associate from earth or with our guardian seraphim, no permanent companion is assigned, but if we arrive alone, a companion welcomes us when we awaken from the last sleep of time [25:8.5]. The receiving companions have reviewed our ascension records beforehand and are well versed in the careers of the arriving pilgrims [25:8.6]. Moreover, an ascender is never assigned a companion of a nature different from his own superuniverse type [25:8.8].

5. Companionship for Those Who Fail

When an ascender fails in the Deity adventure in Havona and must return to the universes of time, one of the Paradise Companions is assigned to go with him, to comfort and encourage him, until he returns to resume the ascent [25:8.9]. If the pilgrim had been accompanied by his guardian seraphim, that seraphim is permitted to volunteer to go back with him [25:8.10]. When only one of two closely associated ascenders succeeds, the successful one is not permitted to go back even if he wishes to; instead a companion accompanies the one who failed, and the successful one teaches on Paradise while awaiting the return of his associate [25:8.11].

Summary

The Morontia Companions provide hospitality, play, and friendship to ascenders in the local universe [25:7.1-3], and the Paradise Companions are angels assigned on Paradise only to be with us [25:8.1-3]. This provision springs from the Creators' understanding that it is not good for man to be alone [25:8.4], and a companion goes even with the pilgrim who fails [25:8.9]. God's plan cares not only for our achievement but even for our loneliness.
